references.text: The original command that Moses, Aaron, and his sons should wash their hands and feet in the bronze basin before entering the tabernacle or approaching the altar.
Describes the placement of the bronze basin between the tent of meeting and the altar, where they washed themselves.
Moses was commanded to bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the tent of meeting and wash them with water as part of the consecration ritual.
Moses brought Aaron and his sons forward and washed them with water at the consecration of the priests.
The New Testament refers to the cleansing of the body with pure water as a picture of the spiritual cleansing we have in Christ, pointing back to the Levitical washing.
Jesus washes the disciples' feet and teaches about the necessity of spiritual cleansing, reflecting the priests' ritual washing.
This is a direct link between the command (Exodus 30:19) and its fulfillment (Exodus 40:31).
A direct parallel showing the connection between the command (40:12) and its fulfillment (40:31).
